From: ClearWave Ops <ops@clearwave.com>

Cc: jessica@clearwave.com
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Immediate: p99 latency spike after your 12e rollout

Hi Laura and team,

We observed a sharp increase in p99 latency across our production traffic starting ~08:40 PDT shortly after the first 10% of Model-12e was routed to our account (deal CW-4312). The symptom: a 2.8x jump in p99 for short prompts (<128 tokens) and many 5–7s tails on conversational flows. This is causing intermittent timeouts in our user flows.

We rolled a small percentage of traffic back locally but the platform variant still shows degraded p99 in the Redwood dashboard. Can you confirm whether Redwood can:

- Immediately roll us back to the previous serving variant (Model-12d) or route to a stable quantized fallback?
- Authorize an SLA grace window while we investigate?

We can provide logs/trace IDs; attaching a short sample of traces from our side. Please advise next steps and an ETA for rollback if possible — this is impacting customers.

Thanks,
Tom Williams
Head of SRE, ClearWave

Tom — thanks for the alert and the traces. I'm escalating this now and proposing an immediate rollback for ClearWave while we root-cause.

Planned immediate actions (executing now):
- Marking ClearWave traffic for rollback to Model-12d at global routing layer (target: 5 min start, 20 min completion).
- Opening an emergency incident (INF-7821) and collecting sampled KV cache traces + kernel selection logs.
- Temporarily enabling tighter traffic caps for short prompt paths to avoid user-visible timeouts.

Requesting authorization from internal ops/serving to proceed with rollback and to grant ClearWave a temporary SLA carveout (target window: 2026-05-05 08:40 -> 2026-05-06 12:00 PDT) while we investigate. Please confirm ASAP.

Markus/Rishi/Monica — can you confirm whether a rollback to 12d is safe w.r.t. schema/weights and whether there are any known incompatibilities for ClearWave's traffic profile? Also include any rollback runbook steps you want executed.

Laura Bennett

On Tue, May 5, 2026 at 09:30, laura_bennett@redwood.ai wrote:
> Markus/Rishi/Monica — can you confirm whether a rollback to 12d is safe w.r.t. schema/weights and whether there are any known incompatibilities for ClearWave's traffic profile?

Quick technical note and recommendation:
- We've pulled the sample traces and compared KV cache hit/miss ratios. There's a sizable increase in KV cache misses for short prompts on streams served by kernel selection path G (introduced in 12e to improve long-context throughput).
- Hypothesis: the kernel selection change produces suboptimal micro-batching behavior for the short-prompt distribution ClearWave runs; this inflates per-request tail latency.
- Immediate mitigation: rollback routing for ClearWave to Model-12d (identical weights, previous kernel path) OR route ClearWave to Model-12e-compat (a preserved compatibility variant with kernel path F).

Rollback notes:
- Safety: rollback to 12d is safe from a weights/IO standpoint for this customer (no schema changes). We should avoid global rollback — scope to ClearWave (routing key) only.
- Runbook excerpt:
  1) Lock customer routing config (no concurrent rollouts).
  2) Set route override to model-12d for customer CW-4312.
  3) Monitor p50/p95/p99 and error rate for 30 minutes; if stable, promote route change to steady state.

I've attached a perf snapshot and kernel log for the affected serving nodes (perf-snapshot-20260505.tar.gz, model-12e-kernel-log.txt).

I'll stand by to execute the route override if Laura authorizes.

—Markus
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

Tom/Jessica — updating you with actions taken and next steps.

What we did:
- At 09:50 PDT on 2026-05-05 we scoped and applied a routing override to send ClearWave traffic back to Model-12d (per Markus' runbook). The rollback completed by 10:12 PDT and we observed p99 reduce from ~2.8x down to baseline within the 20-minute monitoring window.
- We have left a compatibility variant (model-12e-compat) offline for further QA.

SLA carveout:
- We will grant ClearWave a one-time SLA grace for the window 2026-05-05 08:40 -> 2026-05-06 12:00 PDT. Your account dashboard will reflect the temporary carveout and our billing team is aware.

Follow-up actions (owners):
- Markus: deeper root-cause analysis (kernel selection heuristics) and a regression test for short-prompt micro-batching (INF-7821).
- Rishi: prepare a quality gate for any future kernel-selection rollouts and add a short-prompt workload in the automated canary.
- Monica (CS): coordinate postmortem and customer note; schedule a 30-min sync for Friday 2026-05-07 10:00 PDT to review findings.

Tom, Jessica — we appreciate the quick flagging. We'll deliver a short postmortem and remediation plan within 72 hours. Let me know if you'd like a rollback timeline note added to your contract or a permanent routing preference.
